clue.text: Disgusted response to wet weather in country

parts.note: bah is an exclamation of disgust or contempt
rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: Someone groans in disgust at a downpour somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Bahrain is an island kingdom in the Persian Gulf, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: British veteran missing daughter's support

parts.note: an oldster is an old person, a veteran

clue.text: Be out to lunch and partake of a singular set of facilities in NW town

indicators.note: in places the toilets inside the town

parts.note: Crewe is a railway town in Cheshire, north-west England
loos are toilets, plural facilities

explanation.surface: Out for lunch, someone uses a single block of toilets in a north-west town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out to lunch' is the idiom for mad, not dining; 'singular' is the grammatical abbreviation S.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean to be slightly crazy or eccentric.

clue.text: Fool shunning wife and colleague

indicators.note: shunning says the wife letter is avoided, so dropped

parts.note: wally is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: An idiot avoids both his wife and his workmate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner or associate on the same side, close to a colleague.

clue.text: Requisite work reportedly on source of energy European ignored

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear the word for work, not see it

parts.note: to knead dough is to work it

indicators.note: ignored says the European letter is dropped

parts.note: fuel is a source of energy

explanation.surface: A necessary job on energy supply where Europe gets overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignored' drops E from FUEL, leaving FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful means necessary, so requisite.

clue.text: Old check not popular for display

parts.note: ex- means former, so old

indicators.note: not tells us the word for popular is removed from the restraining word

parts.note: to inhibit is to check or restrain
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned check pattern has fallen out of favour as a design for display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' is the verb restrain, not a fabric pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: An exhibit is an object put on show in a museum or a court, a display.

clue.text: School in awful need — mate's involved in it?

indicators.note: in puts the school inside the jumbled letters
awful suggests the letters of need are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A school in desperate need, with a friend caught up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is whales, not pupils, and 'mate' is checkmate, not a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final phase of a chess game, where checkmate is delivered.

clue.text: Flog piece of ham and fish

parts.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone sells a bit of ham and some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flog' looks like 'sell'; here it means beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide someone is to thrash them, as in tanning their hide, so to flog.

clue.text: Nimble sheep in a ramshackle landholding originally — one follows a lead?

indicators.note: ramshackle suggests the letters are tumbled into disorder
originally tells us to take the opening letter of landholding

explanation.surface: Agile sheep on a rundown farm, one of them trailing after a leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives BLENHEIMSPANIE; the L of 'landholding' ends it. The definition puns on a dog walked on a lead.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blenheim spaniel is a breed of toy dog, and a dog walks behind its owner on a leash.

clue.text: Good man with graduate detained by figure in measure against nuclear weapons

indicators.note: detained by says the man and graduate are held inside the figure

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure
St, for saint, is a good man
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A decent man and a graduate held by a number in some anti-nuclear effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A test ban treaty prohibits trial detonations of atomic bombs, an arms control measure.

clue.text: Short book by the Spanish teacher possibly needs section showing sound attitude?

parts.note: Lev is the short form of Leviticus, a book of the Bible
el is Spanish for the
a head teacher is one example of a teacher, so possibly

indicators.note: showing here is read as putting on a new show of the letters, a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: A short textbook, a Spanish teacher and a section on a sound attitude: it reads like a school curriculum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' rearranges NEEDS plus S into EDNESS. The question mark flags that 'sound attitude' is a loose, playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being level-headed means being calm and sensible, so the quality is a sound, balanced attitude.

clue.text: Set lines are used by this place for selling given backing

definitions.text: Set lines are used by this

indicators.note: given backing tells us the market word is read from right to left

parts.note: a mart is a market, a place for selling

explanation.surface: A trader's pitch is backed by fixed lines of some kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the clue's first half: a vehicle that runs on fixed rails, its set lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams run on fixed rails laid in the street, so they use set lines.

clue.text: Ancient King left rejected parts?

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, famous for Offa's Dyke

explanation.surface: An ancient king left behind whatever was rejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and organs of a butchered animal, once regarded as waste parts thrown out.

clue.text: Swimmer in sports institution preferring hotel to lake

indicators.note: preferring hotel to lake means the hotel letter replaces the lake letter

parts.note: a club is a sports organisation
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A swimmer at a sports club would rather stay at the hotel than swim in the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: The chub is a freshwater fish, and fish are swimmers in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Habitual character engaged in diet hospitalised

indicators.note: engaged in says the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A person's usual nature shows in their hospital diet.

clue.text: What makes bane inane in hollow place?

parts.note: writing the letter B as the word in is what turns bane into inane, so that instruction spells the answer

explanation.surface: A riddle about what turns a curse silly, set in a hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as 'B as IN': swap the B of 'bane' for IN and you get 'inane'.
explanation.definitionFit: A basin is a bowl-shaped depression in the land, a hollow.

clue.text: Musical performance recalled in full at ice rink

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A musical show is remembered as having packed out an ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks LATICER inside 'full at ice rink'; 'recalled' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A recital is a concert given by a soloist or small group, a musical performance.

clue.text: Story right off providing joy

indicators.note: off says the letter for right is taken away from the story word

parts.note: a relation is an account or story

explanation.surface: A tale with the right turned off still brings joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration, a synonym for joy.

clue.text: Hard reference work? Recognise set of steps to follow

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
to own is to admit or acknowledge

explanation.surface: A tough reference book, then an instruction to learn a dance routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoedown is a lively American folk dance, a set of steps danced together.

clue.text: Dish grabbing son in popular nightclub

indicators.note: grabbing says the dish takes the son letter inside it

parts.note: a hotpot is a stew, a dish

explanation.surface: A dish snatches a boy at a trendy club.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancashire hotpot is a British meat and potato stew.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotspot is a lively, fashionable place of entertainment such as a busy club.

clue.text: A form of justice is evident after uprising of Home Counties chaps

indicators.note: after says the word is follows the turned piece
uprising, in a down entry, means the counties and chaps are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: SE, south-east, stands for the Home Counties around London
men are chaps

explanation.surface: Justice is seen to be done after a rebellion by men from around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis is retribution, deserved punishment, in Greek myth the goddess of vengeance.

clue.text: Wine not half knocking out American in gallery — and port

indicators.note: in places the shortened wine inside the reduced gallery
knocking out says the letter for American is removed from the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a London art gallery

indicators.note: not half says only the first half of the wine's name is kept

parts.note: Riesling is a white wine grape and wine

explanation.surface: Half a bottle of wine knocks out an American visitor in an art gallery, and then there's port too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' is a harbour city, not the fortified wine the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Trieste is a major Adriatic seaport in north-east Italy.

clue.text: Old doctor probing many on reflection in house

indicators.note: probing says the old doctor goes inside the reversed many
on reflection says the word for many is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: a lot means many
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns A LOT into TOLA, and 'probing' puts OMB inside. 'house' is the game, not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: House, or housey-housey, is a bingo-type game, and tombola is a similar lottery game.

clue.text: Unorthodox medicine I eliminated is widespread

eliminated says the I is taken out of the mix

explanation.surface: Alternative medicine with the ego removed is now common.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemic means prevalent in a particular place or population, so widespread there.

clue.text: List charge against opponent

a jousting knight's run at an opponent with a lance

explanation.surface: A list of charges laid against a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a lean to one side and a jousting knight's lance charge go by this word.

clue.text: Retired religious teacher taking mass for week for prayer leaders

clue.text: African country with borders obscured getting stick

parts.note: Rwanda is a country in central Africa

clue.text: Impression from high-pitched noise Queen emitted

clue.text: Item to cut by the sound of it

clue.text: Finalise proms so fantastically — evidence of a qualified person?

clue.text: Order is given about nucleus of Everest climbers' network
